Bug: Emoji modifiers in text treated separately when using backspace
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- Also please test using the latest insiders build to make sure your issue has not already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->

<!-- Use Help > Report Issue to prefill these. -->
- VSCode Version: All recent versions, maybe all versions, including Monaco outside of VSCode
- OS Version: macOS, Windows, likely Linux and all others

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Enter an Emoji with a modifier, such as a Fitzpatrick skin type modifier: 👶🏾
2. Hit backspace after that character
3. According to the Unicode specification the entire character should be removed.
4. VSCode removes the modifier and leaves the Emoji, producing 👶

The relevant spec, [UTS #51](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr51/#valid-emoji-tag-sequences), states that:

> A supported emoji modifier sequence should be treated as a single grapheme cluster for editing purposes (cursor moment, deletion, and so on); word break, line break, and so on.

This is probably related to #19390, directly to [a comment about ⚠️](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/19390#issuecomment-399767433), but separate enough that I suppose it warrants its own issue.

It's worth noting that aspects of this work as expected. The editor won't let you select he modifier - it correctly forces you to select the modifier plus the Emoji it modifies as an atomic whole. As reported in #19390 though it's possible to move the cursor inside the modified grapheme cluster and break it. (While the cursor bug doesn't appear in the Monaco playground the backspace bug does).

<!-- Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes
I’ll trace the editor’s grapheme-boundary and delete logic, then make the smallest targeted fix and run the relevant tests.

tools.command: pwd && rg -n "grapheme|Grapheme|emoji modifier|Intl\.Segmenter|Fitzpatrick" -S . -g '!**/node_modules/**' -g '!**/.git/**' | head -n 160

sed -n '410,570p' src/vs/editor/common/controller/cursorCommon.ts && sed -n '450,570p' src/vs/base/common/strings.ts && sed -n '920,1025p' src/vs/base/common/strings.ts && sed -n '850,920p' src/vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursor.test.ts && sed -n '390,455p' src/vs/base/test/common/strings.test.ts

rg -n "1F3FB|Emoji_Modifier|Extended_Pictographic|GraphemeBreakProperty" src/vs/base/common/strings.ts build scripts test -g '!**/node_modules/**' | head -n 100 && rg -n "deleteLeft|DeleteLeft|Backspace|prevCharLength" src/vs/editor -g '*.ts' | head -n 160 && git status --short

sed -n '120,250p' src/vs/editor/common/controller/cursorDeleteOperations.ts && sed -n '1330,1390p' src/vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursor.test.ts && sed -n '1060,1140p' src/vs/base/common/strings.ts && rg -n "nextCharLength|prevCharLength" src/vs/base/test src/vs/editor/test -g '*.ts'

sed -n '1620,1690p' src/vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursor.test.ts && sed -n '5360,5430p' src/vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursor.test.ts && sed -n '1,80p' src/vs/editor/common/controller/cursorDeleteOperations.ts && rg -n '"test:browser"|cursor\.test|test-browser' package.json build -g '*.json' -g '*.js' | head -n 100
sed -n '1,95p' src/vs/editor/common/controller/cursorMoveOperations.ts && sed -n '1,80p' package.json && ls test/unit/browser | head && sed -n '1,140p' test/unit/browser/index.js

rg -n "decreasePositionInModelBy1Column" src/vs -g '*.ts' && sed -n '90,190p' src/vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursor.test.ts && rg -n "function usingCursor|const usingCursor|function moveTo" src/vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursor.test.ts | head -n 30

steps.text: The root cause is isolated: cursor movement already uses grapheme-aware lengths, but Backspace still subtracts one UTF‑16 code unit. I’m aligning deletion with the existing movement behavior and adding a regression test.
